observations: 61-key electronic keyboard with a black plastic body.
Brand 'YAMAHA' is visible in the center of the front panel and on the rear.
Model 'PSR-19' is printed on the top left of the front panel in photo 0.
Control panel includes a numeric keypad, a small LED display, and color-coded voice/style lists in purple and teal.
Rear panel shows ports for 'PHONES/OUTPUT' and 'DC 9-12V IN' in photo 1.
A watermark 'LUCKY SOUNDS SERVICES LTD' is present on all three images.
The keyboard is resting on a red plastic chair; no accessories like a stand or music rest are visible.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the model is a PSR-19, which is a vintage entry-level home keyboard from 1990, not a professional-grade instrument.
The photos are static and do not demonstrate functionality.
No power adapter is shown in the provided photos.
Requires a video of all keys being played to confirm.
Requires a video with audio to confirm the absence of static or distortion.

risks.risk: Functional failure of keys or internal electronics.
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard powered on and every key played in sequence.
A photo of the adapter showing its specifications and it connected to the keyboard.

risks.risk: Audio output defects (speaker crackle or jack issues).
risks.proof: A video with clear audio demonstrating the sound at various volumes.

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard being powered on and all keys/buttons tested.
Photo of the included power adapter.
Clearer photo of the display screen while powered on.
response.reason: The item is a vintage Yamaha PSR-19. While the seller claims it works, there is no visual proof. It is priced at the bottom of the market range for Yamaha keyboards due to its age and unverified status.
